tags.gist: Agrees GenAI differences are captured and calls the matrix a starting point, adding that a prior authorization should not be assumed to survive material change.
Proposes an execution-time Lookback and Revalidation control on any material change, yielding act, suspend or escalate, with failures placing the function on hold.
Asks FDA to add execution-time authorization integrity as a mandatory gate, since benchmarking, monitoring and PCCPs do not show a system may act now.
Maps Q1 to adding a mandatory gate on execution-time authorization integrity covering reversibility, traceability and valid human authority.
Maps Q5 to treating a conversation as system state that changes, detecting directive drift and revalidating before consequential output.
Maps Q18 to Q20 to event-triggered reassessment, independent supervisory controls, fail-closed behavior and governed returns.
Maps Q21 to defining authority lineage and duties for each role without diffusing manufacturer accountability.
Maps Q22 to Q24 to tiering changes by materiality, revalidating before use and holding when scope or impact is unestablished.
Maps Q25 to version-linked, current, decision-relevant model information with sponsor responsibility for intended-use validation retained.
Maps Q26 to limiting tools and routes, prohibiting self-authorization, requiring human checkpoints for high-consequence actions and reconciling afterward.
Wants the framework to evaluate execution-time authorization integrity separately as a pass, hold or escalate gate, testing reversibility, time pressure, traceability and scope.
Wants the accumulated conversation state treated as the regulatory object, with manufacturers defining and detecting material trajectory changes that trigger revalidation.
Wants evaluation to include long, contradictory and interrupted conversations with delayed disclosures, separating data, interpretation, uncertainty and context.
Would allow more postmarket reliance only when uncertainty is bounded, harm reversible and monitoring validated before deployment, with less tolerance for irreversible actions.
Wants a defined cadence plus event triggers spanning version, population, output-pattern, evidence and monitoring-loss events, each with owner and response time.
Wants supervisory agents separated from the acting function, with limited permissions, immutable logs, fail-closed behavior and no self-approved modification.
Wants an authority-lineage record and a role matrix for who monitors, pauses, investigates and reports, with the manufacturer keeping system-level accountability.
Wants every modification to pass a materiality determination across all components, in three tiers, with PCCPs prespecifying categories but never redefining their own scope.
Wants pinning or controlled updates, contractual notice, integrity checks, fallbacks and suspension capability, treating any opaque upstream change as material.
Says a master file helps only if current, version-specific and timely, never replacing manufacturer validation, with verifiable linkage to the deployed version.
Wants the whole action chain governed: parent-controlled orchestration, least-privilege tools, fresh human confirmation before irreversible acts, safe-state on failures, reconciliation after.
Wants a compact version-linked record per consequential pathway: authorized baseline, change, authority lineage, lookback and revalidation decisions, reconciliation.
Concludes FDA should require a documented gate for changes, with Lookback and Revalidation, so silence or unavailable authority never counts as permission.
